title: Nice to meet you!
text:
Nice to meet you!
I am currently a 4th year at Case Western Reserve University from New York City pursuing a degree in Computer Science, along with a Master’s in Biostatistics through an integrated program. I am particularly interested in the combination of biology and data analysis, specifically utilizing computational algorithms to gain further knowledge in the molecular mechanisms underlying disease progression and transmission.
This past summer, I interned at Amazon Web Services (AWS) on the Invoice Compliance team. My project focused on developing a data-visualization website that enabled the team to quickly search for individual invoices and identify issues without having to manually sift through large amounts of data, as well as give statistic summaries so that the stakeholders could make quick and informed decisions.
Outside of my academic endeavors, I love to dance, serving as the Treasurer of my collegiate dance team, working to manage our budget and oversee the operations of all the events, successfully raising money to support our team’s travel to out of state dance competitions. I also love to travel with my roommate. Together, we have traveled to so many new cities, learning more about the culture, exploring our palettes, and trying new things.
I am eager to further advance both my academic and professional journey, gaining both knowledge and experience along the way. Please feel free to contact me at contact me.

title: Projects
text:

Over the centuries, I have devoted countless hours to deciphering and translating the ancient scripts and dialects of the various peoples of Middle-earth. My goal is to gain a deeper understanding of the cultures and histories of these peoples by studying their languages. Currently, I am working on a monograph that explores the linguistic roots of the Elvish languages. Through extensive research and analysis, I hope to shed light on the connections between the different dialects of Elvish and their origins. This project has been particularly challenging, as Elvish is a complex and nuanced language, but I am determined to see it through to completion.

title: Blog
text:
March 16, 2026
After reading Jeff Leek’s How To Be A Modern Scientist, I learned a lot from him. Currently as a student, I think that breaking into the academia world is incredibly daunting. However, from reading Leek’s work I came out with a couple of takeaways.
The first being that post publication work is just as important. Even after publishing into a journal, there is still a lot of work that needs to be done. I had originally thought that the end goal was just to get published. However, publishing into a journal does not automatically mean that everyone has read it and so you have to continue advertising it and sharing the results.
The second being the emphasize on peer review. Work should not be completely one sided, but instead we should be asking others for their opinions so that we can put out the best paper possible. The structure that Leek spoke on was: comments to authors, comments to editors, and recommendations. This makes it very clear on what can be done to better the paper. As an added bonus to that, I think that it is very important for a scientist to be able to take criticism well, because peers are doing us a favor by reading our work and trying to make it better. There is no point in being offended by their good will since the end goal for everyone is to come out with a well written and scientifically based paper.
